summary: Lucid trimmed its workforce as part of a broader cost-cutting push across EV manufacturing. The company said the reductions were concentrated in manufacturing and corporate roles.
body: Lucid Motors announced on June 14 that it is cutting about 18% of its workforce, or roughly 1,200 employees, as part of a cost-reduction plan aimed at extending its cash runway. The company said the reductions are concentrated at its Casa Grande, Arizona manufacturing plant and in corporate functions.

In a filing, Lucid attributed the cuts to slower-than-expected demand for its Air and Gravity models and rising input costs for battery materials. The company said it still expects to hit its full-year production target, but with a smaller, more consolidated workforce.

Lucid's stock fell nearly 9% in the days following the announcement. The company said affected employees would receive a minimum of twelve weeks of severance pay and continued benefits coverage through the transition period.
